findings.where: Desktop first screen: the 'Write to me' margin note, the page's one action (p6), set small and slanted in the narrow left gutter, outside the margin line and below the hero copy
findings.fault: The one action has the least visual weight on the first screen. The heading, the clipped photo and the large aqueduct sketch all outweigh it, and it sits in the gutter, where a reader's eye does not go. A squint finds no action at all. On the phone it sits in the column and is found.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer who has decided Mark fits has to hunt for how to reach him. Mark would object too, because getting in touch is the site's whole job.

findings.where: Nav bar (binding strip), the home link: the arches mark and the 'MMM INFRA' wordmark, at both widths
findings.fault: The logo is recoloured. The arches and the wordmark are canary yellow on the binding brown, where the logo's own colours are #404040 and #0070C0. The lockup also drops 'Moseley Infrastructure Advisory Services'. No palette swatch holds the logo blue, either as a token or declared logo-only.
findings.who_objects: Mark: the brief says his logo stays and is never redrawn. A recoloured, cut-down mark is a version he does not hold and has not approved.

findings.where: Palette: 'Ballpoint' #1B2A6B against 'Light hand' #34407A, as used in the hero's italic line ('Over 40 years…') and the sketch hatching next to ballpoint type
findings.fault: The two navies are close enough to read as one ink that came out slightly uneven, not as two inks with two jobs. The 'asides' line looks like the same pen, not a quieter hand.
findings.who_objects: The layout and animation rounds, which have to draw inside this palette. Two near-identical inks invite a mix-up and give no visible rank.

findings.where: Hero: the margin rule (the double line down the pad), against the palette's 'Margin red — margin, note' swatch and the direction card's 'double red margin line'
findings.fault: The margin line is drawn in a dark olive-brown, not the margin red the tile names for it. The tile's own palette and its texture contradict each other, and the pad loses the red line that marks it as a legal pad.
findings.who_objects: Mark, who asked for the legal pad, and the next round's designers, who cannot tell which colour is meant.

findings.where: Type set to the 32 px feint: the hero heading (desktop and phone), the article heading 'The World's Best Public-Private Partnership Law' (desktop 64 px line pitch), and the handwritten pull quote (both widths)
findings.fault: Snapping every block to the feints works against the type. The ruled lines run through the middle of the 64 px hero heading's letters, like a strike-through. The smaller article heading and the script quote are spread to double spacing, so each reads as separate lines, not one phrase. On the phone the quote breaks into four lines with a feint's gap between each.
findings.who_objects: A reader of an article page, who meets a heading and a quote that fall apart. Mark, whose name in the hero looks struck through.

findings.where: Article specimen: the pull quote set in Nanum Pen, against 'Write to me' in the hero, also in Nanum Pen
findings.fault: The hand means two things. In the hero it is the call to action; in the article it is a quote. That breaks the tile's own rule, 'one note per view, the call to action in the margin, never body text', and it weakens the hand as the sign of the one action.
findings.who_objects: A visitor who learns 'Mark's hand = write to me' and then finds it on a quote. Angélique, who is given a rule the specimen itself does not keep.

findings.where: Hero, the italic line 'Over 40 years of international infrastructure experience.'
findings.fault: The hero proves standing with a size word, not checkable work, and no region of work is named anywhere on the first screen.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank procurement officer, who weighs relevant experience by project type and region and discounts year counts. The brief also asks for 'one strong line, no boasts'.

findings.where: Contact route: 'Write to me' (p6, mailto only) and the nav's 'Contact' (p5, links to #); there is no footer anywhere, though the palette names Binding for 'nav, footer'
findings.fault: The email address is never shown as text. 'Write to me' works only where a mail client is set up, and the nav's Contact goes nowhere. There is no footer to carry the address on every page, so on many work machines there is no working way to reach Mark.
findings.who_objects: A visitor on a locked-down agency PC with webmail: they click, get nothing, and have no address to copy.

findings.where: Article specimen: the lecture row 'Streamlining the PPP Process…' with 'Lecture · 23 April 2026 · PDF' beside it, at both widths
findings.fault: The meta column is too narrow, so even at 1440 px it wraps over two lines and on the phone over three. The row's bottom rule collides with the title's underline and the meta's last line, so the link underline and the divider merge into one line.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for Mark's talks, who sees a cramped, untidy row in the one place a publication is listed.

findings.where: Motion sketch: 'Replay the note' (p10, a button)
findings.fault: The button looks exactly like a prose link (underlined body text), so it borrows the link's signifier for something that acts in place.
findings.who_objects: A designer reading the tile as the button specimen, which is also missing: the tile's brief asks for a button, and this is the only one shown.

findings.where: Motion sketch timeline table on the phone
findings.fault: The four-column table squeezes the Element column to a few words a line, so a single row runs to ten lines and is hard to read.
findings.who_objects: Mark or the founder reviewing the tile on a phone.
